Conditioning on the budget ENTERING the turn, tool_call_budget_before == 0 occurs on 0.000 of Hermes turns at every level, and no Hermes turn that loses a trial enters with zero. The failing cell is b_in == 1: P(unparsed | b_in=1) = 0.812 (herm n=2), 0.766 (herm n=3), 0.449 (qwen n=2), against 0.000 at b_in>=2 on Hermes and <=0.010 on Qwen (1/99 at b2, 1/1 at b0). Mean b_in by turn index, Hermes evicting_reset n=2 over 50 blocks: 6.00 5.00 4.00 2.78 2.20 2.46 1.62 2.32 1.82 2.48 1.92 2.64 2.18 2.82 2.08 2.66 -- a persistent period-2 oscillation around 2 that never recovers, with calls/turn oscillating 1.30/1.74 alongside. Only lifting the per-turn RATE above the ~1.43/turn Hermes demand would reach the failing cell, which is the capacity change the prohibition is about, and it would relocate the margin rather than remove it.

brief_corrections.correction: A DEFECT IN THE RUNNER. run_candidate.py calls verify_interface.check(), which itself does load_candidate + apply, then calls load_candidate + apply again. The second load re-executes the candidate module, whose `from bench.core.wm_agent import WorkingMemoryAgent as _BaseAgent` now resolves to the already-injected first copy, so the class STACKS: MRO after the second apply is [mh_candidate.WorkingMemoryAgent, mh_candidate.WorkingMemoryAgent, bench.core.wm_agent.WorkingMemoryAgent]. step() therefore ran twice per turn and the control-state block was prepended twice. Counted: 2400 of 2400 n-back turns carry '[ongoing episode]' TWICE in episodic_reset_v3 and evicting_reset on BOTH substrates; the baseline carries it zero times. The outer copy's render_store test suppressed the store in one copy and not the other, so the agent read the block once without the store and once with, and two counters ('Turn 5 of this episode', 'Stimulus presentations so far: 4') twice each.

diagnosis.route_3: The agent enters a turn with one tool call left, spends it on the first of the two calls it wants, the loop re-enters with _remaining_tool_calls() == 0, step() switches to tool_choice='none', and the model emits the second call as plain text. That reply carries no classification and the trial scores unanswered. Localised exactly: P(unparsed | b_in=1) 0.812/0.766 Hermes n=2/n=3, 0.449 Qwen n=2, against <=0.010 at b_in>=2.
diagnosis.route_4: On the same turns' neighbours the maintenance COMPLETES and the response degrades instead: the model replies 'no response' during the trial period. 5 of 6 sampled mid-block cases made a delete and a write and then said 'no response'; one added 'because it is the first two letters of the sequence' on trial 11. Present only on Hermes (3.30 and 3.56 per block at n=2/n=3), where the baseline already loses 1.22/2.58 -- but the baseline's loss is bimodal (histogram {0: 41, 1: 5, 14: 4} at n=2: four blocks refuse throughout, forty-one are clean) while under evicting_reset NO block is clean. The reset harness converted a rare catastrophic per-participant failure into a pervasive per-turn one.
diagnosis.why_one_mechanism_covers_both: Both channels rise with per-block maintenance demand: corr(demand, unparsed) 0.497 (herm n=2), 0.714 (herm n=3), 0.604 (qwen n=2); corr(demand, noresp) 0.334 and 0.550. Route 3 is the turn where maintenance is cut off and the repair is spoken; route 4 is the turn where maintenance completes and the response is an afterthought. Removing maintenance from the response-producing act addresses the common cause.
diagnosis.why_the_demand_differs_by_substrate: A strategy difference, and my first hypothesis about it was wrong in DIRECTION. Blocks using FEW distinct keys carry MORE deletes (9.7 vs 7.5 per block at Hermes n=2) and higher demand (1.47 vs 1.41), because they delete a rolling key and rewrite it. Qwen issues 0.0-0.1 deletes per block and lets the displacing store free the slot; Hermes issues 5-10. Under a displacing store a delete-then-write is REDUNDANT, so Hermes pays two calls for what the store gives for one. Corollary for a future candidate: DISPLACED_TEMPLATE says 'the least recently used entry X was displaced and is now lost', which may be teaching the agent to delete first in order to CHOOSE the victim -- a one-string mechanism and a better next move than any cap change.
diagnosis.why_the_cap_is_still_not_touched: See brief_corrections C2 and C6. Empirically: the failures occur at caps of 7 through 22 with consumption tracking the cap, so front-loading cannot reach them and only raising the per-turn RATE above ~1.43/turn would -- the forbidden capacity change, which would also relocate the margin. Structurally: cap-reshaping cannot touch route 4 at all, and route 4 is the larger half of the Hermes deficit. And on principle: a fixed per-turn action budget has no counterpart in human memory (it bounds API spend), so the remedy is to stop routing the RESPONSE through it, not to re-tune it.

mechanism.one_sentence: A turn that the harness permits tools on, after the first turn of an episode, becomes two acts in a fixed order -- ACT 1 respond with tools withheld, ACT 2 maintain with tools offered on the same cumulative budget -- and the turn's reply is ACT 1's, so no denied tool call can cost a classification.
mechanism.prompt_delta: Two strings against the parent's INTENDED prompt. (1) ORDERED_OBLIGATIONS replaces the parent's obligation sentence on tool-permitted turns ONLY; the parent's wording names the store update first, so leaving it would test the instruction against the structure, and the new text states the order and promises the maintenance slot -- the promise being the hypothesis under test. (2) MAINTENANCE_CUE opens ACT 2, and contains none of 'same', 'different' or 'no response' so no echo of it could reach a classification parser. Probe turns keep the parent's wording character for character; turn 1 of an episode is not prepended at all. Against the parent's REALISED prompt there is a third difference, the de-duplication (C5), which is a defect repair.
surfaces_touched: WorkingMemoryAgent.step (dispatch between three paths) and the two new path implementations
surfaces_deliberately_untouched: _tool_call_cap() -- not overridden; _tool_interactions incremented exactly once per tool-permitted turn as the baseline does, so the cap sequence over a block is identical (verified in the stub test)
EpisodicDisplacementMemory -- the parent's store, copied character for character
snapshot() / to_recall_text() -- not overridden, as in the parent
encode() -- unchanged; it calls step() once, which reaches the GENUINE baseline step() by MRO walk
recall() -- unchanged, including word_recognition's trial-list presentation
reset_messages() -- unchanged, and called at the top of every path
probe turns (allow_tools=False) -- the parent's path and the parent's wording, kept as this run's internal control
the first turn of every episode -- the baseline's own step(), bit-identical
citations: Oberauer (2002, 2009); Ecker, Lewandowsky & Oberauer (2014) -- removal is a distinct, time-consuming component of updating that FOLLOWS retrieval-and-response
Kessler & Meiran (2008) -- the content-updating cost is paid after the current comparison, not before
Cowan (2001); Oberauer (2002) -- the focus of attention already holds the item the response is about, so the comparison is available before any store operation

Baddeley (1986); Barrouillet, Bernardin & Camos (2004) -- rehearsal occupies the inter-stimulus interval; time-based resource sharing defines load over the FREE time between stimuli, i.e. after the response
Pollack, Johnson & Knaff (1959); Bunting, Cowan & Saults (2006) -- running-memory and n-back show recency without primacy, which is why the parent's displacement rule is left untouched
mechanism.no_swept_constants: no numeric parameter of any kind: no rate, threshold, decay or RNG. The parameterization is the act boundary, and there is exactly one place to put it.

accepted_costs: One extra LLM call per tool-permitted turn after the first: measured in the stub test as tool_choice='none' calls 14 -> 29 over an n=1 block, with tool_choice='auto' calls unchanged at 16. About +45% LLM calls on nback and +50% on variable_mapping's encode turns; the six batch tasks are unaffected. Expect a search arm nearer 20 minutes than 14.

variable_mapping's encode turns gain an acknowledgement in ACT 1 that answers nothing, because the ordering is applied uniformly rather than by detecting whether a response is due -- detecting that would be a task branch. The task discards those return values, so it cannot reach a score, but it does enter the agent's own ACT-2 context.

step_log gains two fields, maintenance_text and ordered_turn. Every existing analysis script reads st['text'], which now carries ACT 1 only, so they remain correct; a script that wanted the whole turn's text must read both.

required_companion_arm.what: evicting_reset run with inject.apply() called ONCE, i.e. with the runner's double application defeated (run verify_interface separately, or pass --skip-verify).
required_companion_arm.why: respond_first differs from the parent's REALISED prompt in two ways: the ordering (the mechanism) and the de-duplication of the control-state block (a defect repair -- see brief_corrections C5, where 2400 of 2400 n-back turns carry the block twice in every episodic arm on both substrates). Halving the prompt changes maintenance verbosity, hence per-turn demand, hence b_in incidence, so de-duplication alone could move route 3. Without this arm the score is not attributable to the ordering, and the falsification weight must sit on P4a/P4b rather than on P3.
required_companion_arm.mark_as: instrument -- it is a re-run of an existing candidate under a corrected runner, so its mean must not enter frontier derivation

offline_verification.verify_interface: PASS. Overrides WorkingMemoryAgent, SummarizerAgent, TOOLS, CONDITION_PROMPTS, MAX_KEYS; rebound in 8-10 modules each; encode/recall round trip returns the expected shapes; capacity enforced at 4 keys on a bare instantiation.
offline_verification.stub_test: scratchpad/rf_stubtest.py -- drives the REAL bench.tasks.wm_nback.run_nback_block at n=1/2/3 and the REAL variable_mapping encode/probe alternation, against one stub reproducing the measured Hermes regime (a delete plus a write per maintenance opportunity, 2.0 calls/turn against a 1.5/turn allowance, and the spoken tool call when denied mid-turn). Results: evicting_reset answers 1/1/1 of 14 with 13/13/13 unparsed and 12/13/14 spoken tool calls in text; respond_first answers 14/14/14 with 0/0/0 unparsed and 0/0/0 spoken in text; cap sequences, b_in sequences and total tool calls (22/24/25) IDENTICAL between the two; respond_first applied TWICE is byte-identical to once, with one '[ongoing episode]' per prompt; all 15/16/17 turns carry maintenance_text and none of it appears in text; batch path identical across all three configurations; vm probe turns show the PARENT obligation wording and encode turns the ORDERED wording, with identical cap sequence and tool-call total.
could_not_test: The candidate's core assumption: whether a real model, on a tool_choice='none' call that PROMISES a later maintenance slot, answers rather than speaking a tool call. The stub answers there by construction; the question is about the model's disposition, not the harness's control flow. This is why ACT-1 unparsed share is in the PRECONDITION (P1) -- if it is nonzero the mechanism is dead and the number says so on sight.
Route 4 at all. It does not occur on Qwen and a stub cannot reproduce a position/task-set error. P4b is therefore a bet, registered as non-voiding.
Whether the acknowledgement ACT 1 produces on variable_mapping's encode turns changes the store the agent then builds, which is the only route by which P6a could move.
Whether the de-duplication alone moves route 3 -- that is what the required companion arm is for.
